summary:
ASTRA Crew Health is an intelligent, research-informed astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew well-being and mission readiness during long-duration space missions.

Unlike traditional monitoring dashboards that focus primarily on displaying measurements, ASTRA brings together physiological trends, crew-reported observations, and mission-specific fitness criteria to support more informed decisions.

ASTRA is a functional research prototype that demonstrates how integrated, explainable health-monitoring software could contribute to safer, more autonomous human space exploration.
details:
ASTRA is a web-based astronaut health monitoring platform that combines several capabilities into one accessible interface.

Explore ASTRA — Interactive Demo Guide

Live Application: https://www.astracrew.health/
Github Repo: https://github.com/dronv/astra-crew-health

ASTRA is a fully interactive prototype. We encourage judges to explore the following features to experience how the platform connects astronaut health monitoring with mission readiness.

  1. Start the Simulation: Navigate to Simulation, start the telemetry simulation, and experiment with different simulation modes. Keep an eye on the Overview and Body Health pages to observe how physiological measurements, health indicators, and alerts respond to changing conditions.
  2. Explore the Interactive Body Map: Open Body Health and click on different body parts in the interactive health map. Explore the cardiovascular, respiratory, neurological, and musculoskeletal information to understand how ASTRA connects physiological monitoring with spaceflight health risks.
  3. Record Daily Health: Navigate to Daily Health, complete the daily wellness form, and submit your observations. Then explore Health Trends to see how recorded information can be tracked and reviewed over time.
  4. Evaluate Mission Readiness: Select Start Self-Assessment, complete the questionnaire, and review the resulting Mission Readiness assessment to see how ASTRA brings together crew-reported information and readiness indicators.

Suggested Demo Flow: Simulation → Overview → Body Health → Daily Health → Health Trends → Self-Assessment → Mission Readiness.

All physiological telemetry is simulated for demonstration purposes.

1. Mission Dashboard

The central dashboard presents astronaut health information, mission context, and a live mission clock, giving users an overview of crew health and operational status.

2. Real-Time Physiological Monitoring

ASTRA uses WebSocket communication to display continuously updating simulated physiological measurements. This demonstrates how future wearable sensors and onboard monitoring systems could provide continuous health information.

3. Health Monitoring and Anomaly Detection

The system evaluates physiological observations and identifies unusual patterns that may warrant additional attention. These assessments are intended to support awareness rather than provide medical diagnoses.

4. Crew Daily Logs and Self-Assessments

Astronauts can record daily wellness information, symptoms, and observations. This allows subjective experiences such as fatigue, sleep quality, and discomfort to be considered alongside physiological measurements.

5. Fitness Assessment

ASTRA incorporates selected requirements from NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1, Revision C, including aerobic capacity, muscular strength, and in-mission fitness retention.

The prototype supports different evaluation criteria for microgravity EVA and lunar or Martian surface EVA scenarios. It also distinguishes missing assessment data from measured results.

6. Mission Readiness

The mission-readiness module presents structured evaluations of selected health and fitness indicators. Its purpose is to help demonstrate how mission-specific requirements and individual baseline measurements could inform operational readiness reviews.

7. Research, Health Awareness & Action Plan

ASTRA uses NASA Human Research Program resources to explain the five hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile or closed environments.

These hazards are connected to cardiovascular, respiratory, cognitive, and musculoskeletal health information.

Technical Architecture

ASTRA was developed using:

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite, and CSS.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Real-Time Communication: WebSockets for live telemetry.
  • Database: SQLite for persistent application information.
  • Data Processing: Python-based physiological analysis and readiness evaluation.
  • Deployment: Vercel for the frontend and Oracle Cloud for the backend.
  • Source Control: Git and GitHub.

The backend generates simulated physiological telemetry and processes health information. The frontend displays real-time observations, assessments, and mission-related information through an interactive dashboard.

Scientific Foundation

NASA research directly influenced ASTRA's design.

NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 informed the prototype's mission-specific aerobic and muscular fitness evaluations.

NASA Human Research Program resources informed the health-awareness content, risk categories, and self-assessment context.

The platform distinguishes measured fitness inputs from simulated telemetry and recognizes that missing information cannot establish fitness readiness.

Innovation and Creativity

ASTRA combines multiple dimensions of astronaut health into a unified, interactive platform rather than presenting physiological measurements in isolation.

Its distinctive features include:

  • Integration of continuous physiological monitoring with crew-reported health information.
  • Mission-specific fitness evaluations for microgravity and planetary surface operations.
  • Research-informed explanations connecting spaceflight hazards to relevant body systems.
  • An accessible prototype demonstrating how health information could support onboard autonomy.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

  • Ideation and Brainstorming
  • Research and information gathering
  • Data analysis and interpretation
  • Coding, debugging and troubleshooting
  • Other Project Related SI use

Potential Impact

As human missions travel farther from Earth, astronauts may need greater independence in monitoring their health and recognizing when additional medical evaluation is appropriate.

ASTRA demonstrates a potential foundation for integrated crew health awareness and decision-support systems.

With further validation and integration, similar approaches could support long-duration exploration missions and other remote environments where immediate medical assistance is limited.
